question: What is a health care provider?

options.B: Only licensed physicians working in government hospitals
options.C: Any individual or institution delivering health services
options.D: Health insurance administrators processing medical claims

explanation: A health care provider encompasses both individuals and facilities offering preventive, curative, or rehabilitative services. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h1)

question: Why must student nurses understand the different types of health care providers?

options.A: To calculate hospital revenue and health insurance tariffs
options.B: To diagnose complex surgical conditions independently
options.C: To improve interprofessional collaboration and patient referral pathways
options.D: To manage pharmaceutical manufacturing plants efficiently

explanation: Knowing provider types helps nurses guide patients effectively through the healthcare system and work well with various team members. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h1)

question: Which facility serves as the usual first point of contact in the healthcare system?
explanation: Primary health care centers are designed to be the initial entry point for basic community health services. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h2)

question: A patient needing open-heart surgery is best managed at which level of care?
explanation: Advanced surgical procedures like open-heart surgery require specialized equipment and personnel found only in tertiary facilities. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h2)

question: What is the main source of funding for public health care providers in Nigeria?
explanation: Public health facilities are primarily financed through public funds allocated by various tiers of government. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h3)

question: What is a major limitation commonly associated with private health care providers?

options.A: They are legally restricted from offering emergency care
options.B: They only operate in rural agricultural communities
options.C: Government regulations prevent them from hiring nurses
options.D: Services can be too expensive for low-income patients

explanation: Private providers rely heavily on user fees, making care potentially unaffordable for vulnerable populations without insurance. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h3)

question: Mission hospitals and faith-based clinics typically belong to which category of providers?
explanation: Faith-based health facilities operate primarily on a charitable or not-for-profit basis to serve communities. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h4)

question: How do for-profit and not-for-profit health organizations differ in handling financial surplus?

options.A: For-profit entities distribute surplus to owners, while not-for-profits reinvest it
options.B: Not-for-profit clinics are prohibited from charging any patient fees
options.C: For-profit hospitals rely entirely on government grants for survival
options.D: Not-for-profit facilities pay high dividends to shareholders

explanation: The defining difference lies in profit distribution versus reinvestment into the organization's health mission. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h4)

question: Which group is classified as an informal health care provider in Nigeria?
explanation: Traditional birth attendants operate outside the orthodox professional training and regulatory framework, making them informal providers. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h5)

question: Why do many patients in rural areas frequently visit informal medicine vendors first?

options.A: Because the government mandates informal care as a first step
options.B: Because orthodox hospitals refuse to treat common illnesses
options.C: To obtain specialized surgical procedures at lower costs
options.D: Due to geographical proximity and immediate availability

explanation: Informal vendors are often embedded within local communities, offering quick access when formal hospitals are far away. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h5)

question: What is the dominant payment method for healthcare in Nigeria?
explanation: Most patients pay directly for services at the point of care because prepayment schemes are not yet universal. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h6)

question: What action should a nurse take when a patient admits to seeing an informal herbalist before coming to the hospital?

options.A: Discontinue all orthodox medical treatments until the herbal remedies finish
options.B: Assess for potential herb-drug interactions and provide non-judgmental education
options.C: Assume the patient will recover fully without needing hospital medication
options.D: Report the patient immediately to hospital security for disciplinary action

explanation: Nurses must safely evaluate previous informal treatments for side effects or drug interactions while educating the patient respectfully. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h6)
